claims.text: PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts can catalyze ethanol oxidation.
Untreated PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts exhibit ethanol-induced surface segregation under reaction conditions.
Ethanol adsorption dynamically restructures the PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst surface.
Adsorption of ethanol and its intermediates preferentially segregates Pt to the catalyst surface.
The extent of dynamic surface restructuring governs ethanol-oxidation selectivity.
A tailored potential-cycling pretreatment can suppress ethanol-induced Pt surface segregation.
Suppressing Pt segregation maintains a more compositionally homogeneous catalyst surface.
Pt surface segregation creates active Pt-containing surface ensembles.
The degree of Pt surface segregation changes the local surface electronic structure, including the d-band center.
Spatially heterogeneous local electronic environments can produce different adsorbate binding energies on high-entropy-alloy surfaces.
Changes in local electronic structure and intermediate binding can influence pathway selection and product selectivity in complex reactions.
Suppressing Pt segregation will alter the balance of adsorbed ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The pretreated catalyst will have a measurably different product distribution from the untreated catalyst.
The product-distribution change can be observed through the acetaldehyde-to-acetic-acid ratio.
Reduced Pt segregation is expected to favor a less oxidative ethanol-oxidation pathway.
The proposed relationship should hold from 25 to 80 °C, from 0.2 to 1.0 V versus RHE, and at fixed ethanol concentration in aqueous electrolyte.
No significant pretreatment-induced difference in either Pt segregation or product distribution would falsify the hypothesis.
